description: Astro Bengalis is a team of space and technology enthusiasts passionate about satellite remote sensing, Earth observation, geospatial intelligence, and AI-driven solutions to real-world challenges.
summary: Delta-SAR is an open-source web platform that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar to see the Jamuna River in Bangladesh through monsoon clouds, mapping floods and riverbank erosion from 13 NISAR GCOV passes (June to October 2026) between Sirajganj and Kazipur. It overlays that change on buildings and cropland: 187-232 ha of riverbank lost at 38 sites, 712 buildings within 100 m of a retreating bank, and 39,425 ha of cropland under water at the July peak. Its Bangla-first resident app, Bonna Sathi, turns fixed radar, river, and rain rules into alerts that a volunteer approves before sending; the phone reads each alert aloud, and families reply "safe" or "help". DeltaSAR helps disaster officials, the Water Development Board, and riverbank families act before the river takes homes, crops, and livestock.
details:
THE CHALLENGE IT ANSWERS

Dancing with the SARs asks for an interactive app that uses NISAR radar to track and explain surface change. Our study area is the Jamuna River from Sirajganj to Kazipur, Bangladesh, a braided river that moves every monsoon. CEGIS estimates the Jamuna alone has eroded about 940 square kilometers of land since 1973, roughly three times the area of Dhaka city. In 2020, it kept Sirajganj underwater for three months, with reported damage of about Tk 300 crore. The worst change happens under thick monsoon clouds, when optical satellites see nothing. NISAR's L-band radar sees through it, day and night.

HOW IT WORKS

1. NISAR first: DeltaSAR reads 13 NISAR L2 GCOV passes on track 069A (18 Jun to 9 Nov 2026) through ASF and NASA Earthdata, and detects each new pass automatically through NASA CMR. Passes before 25 Oct are labelled PROVISIONAL.

2. Water and bank change: HH and HV backscatter are converted to dB and thresholded into a water mask for every pass, with the threshold recalibrated on each new pass. HH separated water from land by 9.0-11.6 dB against 6.8-8.2 dB in HV, so HH drives the mask. Comparing masks over time gives new water, receded water, and bankline retreat.

3. Impact: change is overlaid on Google Open Buildings, ESA WorldCover cropland, and JRC Global Surface Water. Between 18 Jun and 4 Oct 2026, the mainland bank lost 187-232 ha at 38 sites; 712 buildings stood within 100 m of a retreating bank; and 39,425 ha of cropland was underwater at the 24 Jul peak.

4. Context: GPM IMERG rainfall, FFWC river levels, GloFAS discharge, and the Copernicus 30 m DEM feed a 7-day flood probability map. Official forecasts remain FFWC's and BMD's.

5. Alerts with a human in the loop: three fixed rules (radar, river, rain) draft an alert, and a volunteer approves it. The Bangla-first resident app, Bonna Sathi, reads it aloud, works offline, and lets families reply "safe" or "help". No AI drafts, approves, or sends an alert.

6. Built to be checked: a source audit recomputes 23 headline numbers from their files on every code change. Daily live tests confirm every NASA connection still works.

WHAT YOU CAN DO IN IT

- Radar explorer: swipe between any two of the 13 passes, add live NASA GIBS layers (OPERA DSWx-S1, MODIS flood, IMERG), and click any point for a report on water, bank change, buildings, and cropland.

- Guided demo: replay the full alert loop on the 24 Jul 2026 peak pass in a private sandbox.

- Ask DeltaSAR: ask in English or Bangla; Gemini answers only from our published facts, and a check flags any number not in our data.

- Methods page: validation, every data source and licence, limits, and live checks of each NASA connection.

WHO IT HELPS

- Families on chars and low banks: approved Bangla voice alerts and a one-button way to ask for help.

- Disaster officials (DDM, district and upazila): where the river flooded or cut in, and which buildings and fields are exposed.

Our economic model, built from official Sirajganj damage reports, estimates that acting early could avoid about Tk 3.0 crore of losses a year for Tk 0.6 crore in running cost (benefit-cost ratio 4.6, moderate case). It counts only losses; timely information can change, such as livestock moved and house materials saved, but not the roads or land.

HONEST LIMITS

Neither our river-stage proxy nor our machine-learning model beat simple persistence at predicting the next pass: NASA also publishes track 069A passes 45-71 hours after acquisition. So DeltaSAR reports observed change and uses it to target warnings; it does not replace official forecasts. Exposure is not damage, and economic results stay scenarios until a pilot measures them.

WHAT WE'D BUILD NEXT

- A one-monsoon pilot with the Department of Disaster Management and BWDB in Sirajganj, measuring how often alerts lead to action.

- Ascending and descending passes together, to shorten the gap between looks during a flood.

- NISAR interferometry to test whether embankment subsidence can be seen before failure.

- Expansion to the Padma and Teesta, and OPERA's NISAR water product (DSWx-NI) once released.
dataRefs: NASA GIBS Layers (OPERA DSWx-S1, OPERA RTC-S1, and MODIS Flood/True Colour)
